label.trigger: A legacy (_ZN-prefixed) symbol that has no closing E is passed to demangle or try_demangle: either the text stops inside an identifier body, for example _ZN3fo (length 3, only two letters), or it ends right after the last complete name, for example a single four-letter name with nothing after it.
label.expected_impact: Running out of characters while skipping an identifier is converted into the closing-E marker instead of an error, so the validator accepts the cut symbol. try_demangle then reports a Rust symbol, demangle picks the legacy style, and formatting it slices beyond the input's last byte and panics (observed for _ZN3fo); a symbol that stops exactly at the end of its last name is printed as a demangled path instead of being returned unchanged.

context_locations.note: The public entry point trusts an Ok from the legacy validator to classify the input as a Rust symbol; only an Err makes it fall back to v0 or to printing the raw text, and try_demangle reports success from this choice.
The formatter walks the element lengths again with unwrap and unchecked slicing, relying on the validator having proved that every declared length fits inside the string.

known_counterevidence.note: Reading the length digits still returns Err when the text ends, so an input that stops right after a length prefix is rejected; only a stop inside or right after the name characters slips through.

label.fix_summary: Treat a missing character in the identifier-skipping loop as a validation failure again (chars.next().ok_or(())? ), so a legacy symbol that ends before its closing E is rejected and shown verbatim.

check.summary: Runs the crate's own unit tests legacy::tests::demangle and tests::demangle, whose assertions require an unterminated legacy input to be refused; the test binary is built with rustc --test from src/lib.rs.

verification.summary: verify --run-checks with rustc 1.99.1 (linker gcc 15.2.0): the unit-test binary built from src/lib.rs with rustc --test fails legacy::tests::demangle and tests::demangle on before (an unterminated input is accepted) and passes both on after. No cargo, no network and no dependencies are used; the workspace members under crates/ and fuzz/ are not built.
